metadataVO.title: 中国1km逐日气象六要素重构产品（1961-2021）
metadataVO.titleEn: China's 1km daily reconstructed product of six meteorological elements (1961–2021)
metadataVO.description: 高分辨率且高精度的气象产品对于深入理解气候变化机制及其在水文、水资源管理和生态环境等相关领域的影响至关重要。本研究提出了一种分层递进式重构框架（HPRF），用于生成高分辨率气象产品。该框架采用多层感知器（MLP）深度学习算法，通过多阶段过程逐步映射中国大陆六个气象要素——平均气温、最高气温、最低气温、大气压力、相对湿度和日照时长——的空间分布，解析这些要素与地形因素（包括纬度、经度和海拔）之间的复杂非线性关系以及要素之间的相互作用。深度学习分层渐进框架（DL-HPRF）能够生成任意所需空间分辨率的逐日气象产品。本研究中，生成了1公里分辨率的产品，并利用118个地面观测站的数据对其质量进行了评估。结果表明，所有重构的气象产品均具有较高的准确性。平均气温、最高气温和最低气温的误差较小（RMSE中位数分别为1.03℃、1.19℃、1.34℃；ME中位数分别为-0.09℃、-0.10℃、-0.08℃），且与地面数据高度一致（CC中位数分别为1.00、0.99、0.99）。大气压力的误差也较小（RMSE中位数为2.48 hPa；ME中位数为-0.02 hPa），一致性较高（CC中位数为0.98）。尽管相对湿度的准确性相较于以上5种产品较低（RMSE中位数为6.02%；ME中位数为-0.5%；CC中位数为0.90），但其精度依然达到了优异标准。日照时长的精度较高（RMSE中位数为1.48小时；ME中位数为0.05小时；CC中位数为0.93），整体产品质量表现优异。进一步对比分析显示，使用地面数据评估网格化气象产品在复杂地形中的准确性存在局限性，本研究的模型在高海拔地区的表现实际上优于地面数据与网格产品评估指标之间的结果，展现了更高的准确性。
metadataVO.instructions:
文件命名：平均气温、最高气温、最低气温、大气压力、相对湿度和日照时长数据都以栅格数据结构存储，文件的名称分别以MLP_yyyymmdd_MeanTEM_predicted.tif、MLP_yyyymmdd_MaxTEM_predicted.tif、MLP_yyyymmdd_MinTEM_predicted.tif、MLP_yyyymmdd_MeanPress_predicted.tif、MLP_yyyymmdd_MeanRHU_predicted.tif和MLP_yyyymmdd_Suntime_predicted.tif的规则进行命名，其中MLP代表模型，yyyymmdd代表年月日，MeanTEM、MaxTEM、MinTEM、MeanPress、MeanRHU、MeanRHU和Suntime分别代表各要素，比如MLP_19980101_MeanTEM_predicted.tif就代表这个栅格文件描述1998年1月1日我国平均气温分布情况。
数据读取方式：该数据集中的所有栅格文件可以直接用GIS软件或其他支持栅格数据的工具进行读取。

metadataVO.nameOfSubmittedPaper: DL-HPRF: A Deep Learning-Based Hierarchical Progressive Reconstruction Framework for Daily Meteorological Elements at Any Resolution

metadataWordVO.title: China's 1km daily reconstructed product of six meteorological elements (1961–2021)
metadataWordVO.description: Fine-scale and accurate meteorological products are essential for understanding the mechanisms of climate change and its impacts on derivative fields, particularly in hydrology, water resources management and ecological environment. This study proposes a hierarchical and progressive framework (HPRF) for reconstructing high-resolution meteorological products. The framework employs the Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) deep learning algorithm in a multi-stage process to progressively map the spatial distribution of six meteorological elements—average temperature, maximum temperature, minimum temperature, atmospheric pressure, relative humidity, and sunshine duration—across mainland China, by decoding the nonlinear relationships between these elements and topographical factors (latitude, longitude, altitude), as well as the interrelationships among the elements themselves. The DL-HPRF allows for the generation of daily meteorological products at any desired spatial resolution. In this study, the products were generated at a 1 km resolution, with in-situ data from 118 observation stations used to assess their quality. Metrics indicate that all reconstructed products exhibit high accuracy. Average, maximum, and minimum temperatures exhibit minimal errors (median RMSEs: 1.03℃, 1.19℃, 1.34℃; median MEs: -0.09℃, -0.10℃, -0.08℃) and high consistency with in-situ data (median CCs: 1.00, 0.99, 0.99). Atmospheric pressure shows minimal error (median RMSE: 2.48 hPa; median ME: -0.02 hPa) and high consistency (median CC: 0.98). Although relative humidity has slightly weaker accuracy (median RMSE: 6.02%; median ME: -0.5%; median CC: 0.90), it still surpasses standard benchmarks. Sunshine duration maintains high precision (median RMSE: 1.48 h; median ME: 0.05 h; median CC: 0.93), demonstrating overall excellent product quality. Further comparison reveals the limitations of using in-situ data to assess the accuracy of gridded meteorological products in complex terrains, showing that the models developed in this study actually achieve higher accuracy in high-altitude areas than the evaluation metrics between in-situ data and gridded products.
metadataWordVO.instructions:
File Naming Convention: The datasets for average temperature, maximum temperature, minimum temperature, atmospheric pressure, relative humidity, and sunshine duration are stored in a raster data structure. The files are named according to the following convention: MLP_yyyymmdd_MeanTEM_predicted.tif, MLP_yyyymmdd_MaxTEM_predicted.tif, MLP_yyyymmdd_MinTEM_predicted.tif, MLP_yyyymmdd_MeanPress_predicted.tif, MLP_yyyymmdd_MeanRHU_predicted.tif, and MLP_yyyymmdd_Suntime_predicted.tif. Here, 'MLP' denotes the model used, 'yyyymmdd' represents the date in the format year-month-day, and 'MeanTEM', 'MaxTEM', 'MinTEM', 'MeanPress', 'MeanRHU', and 'Suntime' correspond to the respective meteorological variables. For example, MLP_19980101_MeanTEM_predicted.tif refers to the raster file representing the distribution of average temperature in China on January 1, 1998.
Data Access: All raster files within this dataset can be directly accessed and utilized with GIS software or any other tools that support raster data.
